Liam to schedule a dedicated performance run (1hr) with Apex infra week of 2026-09-06
Maya to send SOC2 and security pack links and confirm retention settings by 2026-08-10

Liam O'Reilly: Set up performance benchmark run and provide runbook (due 2026-09-10)

summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, unit costs, reliability incidents, and alignment on roadmap + pilot scope. Customer sees steady increase in embedding usage, concerned about token cost spikes and a recent regional latency blip. Redwood team recommended batching and prefix caching, and proposed a performance run on dedicated capacity for high-throughput endpoints. Action items include cost breakdown, security docs, and a follow-up benchmark run.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-08-05 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Jordan Patel, Maya Chen, Liam O'Reilly (Redwood); Rachel Moore, Diego Fernandez, Sana Malik (Apex Systems)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, I think we have full house, Apex team, welcome - this is the Q3 QBR and health check, we'll run through usage, costs, reliability, and next steps. Maya, do you want to kick off?
[00:00:12] Maya Chen: Yeah, thanks Jordan. Hi Rachel, Diego, Sana. Quick agenda - usage trends, cost drivers, any incidents, and then roadmap. We'll leave time for questions.
[00:00:25] Rachel Moore: Thanks. We mainly want to understand the cost spike in July and the latency blip in EU-west on the 21st. Also, we're evaluating dedicated capacity for our recommendations engine.
[00:00:38] Diego Fernandez: And I want to confirm retention and KMS integration details, plus any networking reqs for VPC.
[00:00:46] Jordan Patel: Great. Quick housekeeping: I'll share the cost dashboard after the call. Liam will speak to the perf stuff.
[00:00:56] Liam O'Reilly: Hi all. So on the perf front, we saw a 120ms median increase in the EU region around 21st - that correlated with a capacity bump and a fallback to a slightly larger model variant, so requests were routed to a compatible model. There was also a KV cash miss - er, KV cache miss - causing more tokens to be re-generated.
[00:01:15] Rachel Moore: When you say fallback, is that automatic routing? We thought we'd pinned v2.1 for our production route.
[00:01:23] Liam O'Reilly: You can pin but our smart routing can still move traffic if the pinned variant is unavailable; in your case there was transient shortage on dedicated nodes in EU-west and traffic briefly routed to a compatible variant with larger context, hence slightly higher latency and token count.
[00:01:40] Sana Malik: Ok - so is the recommendation to move to Dedicated? We're worried about cost.
[00:01:46] Jordan Patel: Good question. There's tradeoffs. Dedicated capacity gives more predictable throughput and fewer fallbacks, so better latency SLOs. However, unit cost per-token can be lower or higher depending on utilization and batching. For your embeddings-heavy workload, batching plus prefix caching can reduce costs significantly.
[00:02:05] Diego Fernandez: Can you quantify "significantly"? Last month token spend was up 38% and finance flagged it.
[00:02:12] Maya Chen: We'll provide a detailed breakdown - average tokens/req, embedding unit counts, and delta vs July. Jordan, I think you have that export.
[00:02:20] Jordan Patel: Yep, I'll send CSV and a slide with top three drivers. Early look: embeddings growth and a couple of routes with very low batching factor (because of timeouts) - bumping the batching window by 50ms increased throughput in our tests without pushing user-perceived latency.
[00:02:37] Rachel Moore: Is that safe for our SLAs? Our product team can't take extra latency.
[00:02:42] Liam O'Reilly: We usually recommend a measured increase - you can preserve p95 latency by applying intelligent batching at the worker level and enabling prefix caching for session-based calls. That's a config change - no code change for most clients.
[00:02:55] Sana Malik: About caching - how does it work with user PII? Some of our prompts include user names.
[00:03:01] Maya Chen: Good flag. Caching can be configured to exclude PII or use hashed keys; also on Private deployments or Dedicated you can enforce customer-managed KMS and TTL policies. We can go over options in the security pack.
[00:03:14] Diego Fernandez: Speaking of security pack, we need SOC two cert, key rotation details, and an HSM/KMS integration guide.
[00:03:22] Jordan Patel: We'll attach SOC2 and the KMS integration notes. Maya will send links.
[00:03:26] Maya Chen: I'll share by Monday, including the retention settings we currently have for hosted accounts.
[00:03:31] Rachel Moore: On reliability, can you walk us through the incident timeline on 21st? Diego - anything else from infra?
[00:03:37] Diego Fernandez: We captured traces - there was a spike in queue depth before the fallback event.
[00:03:40] Liam O'Reilly: Right, timeline: 14:07 UTC - increased queue depth on EU-west pool; 14:09 fallback triggered to variant v2.4-compatible; 14:12 traffic normalized after autoscale and route healing. Root cause: an unexpected model load on a subset of dedicated pools from our side. We pushed a change to routing policy to be more conservative on fallbacks.
[00:03:58] Rachel Moore: How frequent are these fallbacks generally? We need an SLA impact number.
[00:04:04] Jordan Patel: Fall back events of this nature are rare - <0.5% of requests monthly for customers at your scale. We'll include the request-level impact in the post-call report and provide per-route p50/p95 before/during/after.
[00:04:19] Sana Malik: About Dedicated - what's the onboarding timeline and cost structure?
[00:04:24] Jordan Patel: Dedicated typically needs a 4-6 week provisioning window depending on region, and reserved capacity pricing with monthly commits. We can do a pilot with a couple of reserved nodes to run your heavy routes, then expand. We'll show modeled costs in the cost breakdown.
[00:04:40] Diego Fernandez: If we do pilot, do you support private networking/VPC peering?
[00:04:45] Liam O'Reilly: Yes, Dedicated or Private supports VPC peering and private control plane options. For on-prem or air-gapped, we also offer a Private deployment package but that's a heavier lift.
[00:04:57] Rachel Moore: Do you have data residency controls for EU-only data?
[00:05:01] Maya Chen: Yep, region pinning and data residency policies available - we'll include the policy doc link.
[00:05:06] Jordan Patel: Quick drilldown on cost drivers: July spike - two main items: embedding volume increase from a new personalization test, and temporary low batching on route /recommend. Also some retries increased token counts by about 7%. We'll send exact numbers.
[00:05:23] Sana Malik: For the personalization test, can we set rate limits or lower precision embeddings to curb cost?
[00:05:29] Liam O'Reilly: You can use quantized model variants for embeddings which reduce cost slightly but might change vector quality. We recommend running an eval set to measure recall drop before switching.
[00:05:40] Rachel Moore: OK, let's plan an eval run. Who owns that?
[00:05:44] Jordan Patel: Liam can run the perf + eval with your sample set - we'll need a small dataset and a window for the run.
[00:05:50] Liam O'Reilly: Yep, I'll coordinate with Diego on infra access and the sample set.
[00:05:55] Diego Fernandez: We'll provide a 10k row sample and test creds in a staging VPC.
[00:05:59] Maya Chen: Great. Next topic: roadmap alignment. Are you still targeting Q4 for recommender full rollout?
[00:06:06] Sana Malik: Yes, Q4 is the goal. We want to finalize whether we go Dedicated for production by Oct.
[00:06:12] Jordan Patel: For Q4 target, suggested plan: August - run cost breakdown + eval; September - pilot on Dedicated for two routes; October - decision and scale. That gives time for provisioning and a canary roll.
[00:06:27] Rachel Moore: That timeline sounds reasonable. Finance wants to see projected monthly spend at 75% and 90% utilization.
[00:06:34] Jordan Patel: We'll model both scenarios in the cost deck.
[00:06:38] Sana Malik: Any blockers on our side?
[00:06:40] Diego Fernandez: We need the SOC2 and clear KMS steps. Also a short runbook for failover expectations.
[00:06:46] Maya Chen: We'll include a one-page runbook doc and the SOC2 link.
[00:06:49] Jordan Patel: I'll recap next steps near the end. Quick Q/A - Rachel: any user-facing quality concerns?
[00:06:57] Rachel Moore: We've seen a handful of hallucinations in product descriptions - not many, but enough to worry product. Is that something Redwood monitors?
[00:07:05] Liam O'Reilly: We have quality monitoring and alerting tied to evals and prompt sets. We can run a regression check against your prompt tests and set up alerts for QA thresholds.
[00:07:16] Sana Malik: Does that require Private deployment?
[00:07:18] Liam O'Reilly: No, it's available in Hosted and Dedicated as part of Redwood Optimize - we can wire up your prompt set and send daily/regression reports.
[00:07:27] Rachel Moore: Nice. For the pilot we want monitoring and a performance SLA.
[00:07:31] Jordan Patel: We'll draft an SLA addendum for the pilot and include observability dashboards.
[00:07:36] Diego Fernandez: One more infra question - is there a way to enforce mandatory TLS between our VPC and Redwood endpoints?
[00:07:42] Maya Chen: TLS is enforced; for Private deployments you can also require mTLS and client certs. We'll include the cert rotation cadence.
[00:07:50] Rachel Moore: Ok good.
[00:07:52] Jordan Patel: We're at 20 minutes - moving through nicely. Any other questions?
[00:08:00] Sana Malik: How about billing granularity - can finance get per-route chargeback?
[00:08:05] Jordan Patel: Yes, we provide per-route cost breakdowns and token-level attribution down to API key. We'll export that for you.
[00:08:12] Rachel Moore: Great.
[00:08:14] Diego Fernandez: Regarding the performance run - will it simulate real traffic patterns? We need to test burst behavior.
[00:08:20] Liam O'Reilly: We'll do a burst test and steady-state test; we'll also test cold-start and KV cache warmup to measure p95 under load.
[00:08:29] Maya Chen: I'll attach a sample runbook for the bench.
[00:08:33] Jordan Patel: Cool. Quick recap and owners: Jordan sends cost breakdown and modeled scenarios (due 2026-08-07); Maya sends SOC2, KMS guide, retention policy (due 2026-08-10); Liam schedules and runs perf+eval with Apex sample (coordinate dates, deliver by 2026-09-10); Sana to confirm Q4 priorities and stakeholders (due 2026-08-14). Anyone not captured?
[00:09:00] Rachel Moore: That captures it. Thanks.
[00:09:03] Jordan Patel: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf run and the pilot planning session.
[00:09:10] Sana Malik: Thanks all.
[00:09:12] Meeting end (approx).

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors ("KV cash" instead of KV cache, "SOC two"), some speaker label noise; links referenced: cost dashboard (link shared post-call), SOC2 cert (link to security pack), perf runbook (attachment).
